overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of the blind spot argument's roots and critics. You'll be asked about the book's relation to Husserl's Crisis and Merleau-Ponty's primacy of perception, what the book adds, and the main critical responses.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: What does Husserl mean by the surreptitious substitution?

options.html: Galileo's deliberate replacement of Aristotle's physics
options.text: Galileo's deliberate replacement of Aristotle's physics
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The substitution isn't a deliberate theory change. It's unnoticed.

options.html: The unnoticed replacement of the lived world by an idealized one
options.text: The unnoticed replacement of the lived world by an idealized one
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The idealized, mathematical world is then taken for true reality.

options.html: The replacement of observation by pure reasoning
options.text: The replacement of observation by pure reasoning
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Science still observes. The substitution concerns what's taken to be real.

options.html: The replacement of one scientific model by a better, newer one
options.text: The replacement of one scientific model by a better, newer one
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The substitution replaces the lifeworld, not an older model.

forms.stemHtml: What does Merleau-Ponty's primacy of perception claim?

options.html: That only perceptions are real, and nothing else exists
options.text: That only perceptions are real, and nothing else exists
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The thesis isn't that everything is perception. It's a claim about foundation.

options.html: That perception is always more accurate than any measurement
options.text: That perception is always more accurate than any measurement
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The thesis concerns foundation, not accuracy.

options.html: That the perceived world is the foundation all knowledge presupposes
options.text: That the perceived world is the foundation all knowledge presupposes
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Science, logic, and value build on a world first given in perception.

options.html: That science should return to pre-modern methods of inquiry
options.text: That science should return to pre-modern methods of inquiry
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty doesn't reject science. He locates its ground.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following does The Blind Spot add to its phenomenological sources? (Select all that apply.)

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Two of the authors are physicists.

options.html: Applications to relativity, quantum mechanics, and biology
options.text: Applications to relativity, quantum mechanics, and biology
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The book applies the argument well beyond Galilean physics.

options.html: Enactive resources, such as autopoiesis and sense-making
options.text: Enactive resources, such as autopoiesis and sense-making
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! These let the book root experience in life.

options.html: A fuller transcendental method than Husserl's
options.text: A fuller transcendental method than Husserl's
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The book sets transcendental method aside.

options.html: A proof that physical theories are false
options.text: A proof that physical theories are false
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The book accepts the physics and criticizes a worldview attached to it.

forms.stemHtml: What is Husserl's image, translating Ideenkleid, for the covering of mathematical idealizations and symbols that science lays over the world of experience? Enter three words.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The garb fits so well that it's taken for the world itself.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Husserl's image is the garb of ideas.

forms.stemHtml: What does Tom Clark charge when he says the book misdescribes scientists' views?

options.html: That scientists reject the idea of objectivity
options.text: That scientists reject the idea of objectivity
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Clark defends objectivity as a worthy goal.
Sorry, that's incorrect. Clark's charge concerns scientists, not Husserl.

options.html: That scientists never use abstract models
options.text: That scientists never use abstract models
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Clark's point is that scientists use models without taking them to replace experience.

options.html: That few scientists think models replace experience
options.text: That few scientists think models replace experience
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! If he's right, the book attacks a straw man.

title: Roots and Critics
